Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Makhrama (RA) fasts during the Battle of Yamaamah

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that during the Battle of Yamaamah he approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Makhrama (RA), who was lying on the ground. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) stopped by him, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Makhrama (RA) asked him whether the time had come to break the fast. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) replied that the time had already come, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Makhrama (RA) said, "Fill some water in that wooden shield so that I may break my fast with it." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) went to a pond which was brimming with water and used his leather shield to scoop up water to fill the wooden shield. However, when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) returned to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Makhrama (RA), he found that he had already passed away.[^2]
The Fast of Hadhrat Awf bin Abi Hayya and the Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Mudrik bin Awf Ahmis states that he was once with Hadhrat Umar (RA) when a messenger from Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin (RA) arrived. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him about the condition of the people, he mentioned those Muslims who had been martyred. He mentioned the names of the martyrs and added that there were many whom he did not recognise. Hadhrat Umar (RA) commented, "But Allaah knows them all." Some people then said that there was a person who had sold his soul. They were referring to Hadhrat Awf bin Abi Hayya Ahmisi, also known as Abu Shubayl. Hadhrat Mudrik bin Awf interjected by saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! These people are of the opinion that uncle of mine threw himself into destruction." Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "They are wrong. In fact, he bought the Aakhirah in exchange for this world." Hadhrat Awf had been fasting on the day that he was wounded. He was still alive when he was removed from the battlefield and refused to drink any water until he eventually passed away (in the state of fasting).[^3]
